sections.overview: The domestic horse is a single-toed grazing mammal shaped by human breeding. Ancient genomes trace most living domestic horses to a western Eurasian steppe lineage that spread about 4,200 years ago. Its expansion replaced many local horse populations across Eurasia. Earlier horse management did not produce most living domestic lineages. People keep horses worldwide for varied roles.
sections.identification: Horses have a long head, mobile ears, maned neck, deep body, and long limbs with one hoof each. Breed variation spans compact ponies to tall draft horses, with different coats and proportions. Adult males are stallions, females mares, young horses foals. Domestic horse size varies widely by breed: roughly 0.9–1.7 m at the shoulder and 227–900 kg across breed types; these are broad breed ranges, not a single species average.
sections.habitat: People keep horses in pastures, paddocks, and stables across the inhabited continents. Their surroundings depend on local land use and husbandry; domestic horses have no single natural range.
sections.diet: Horses graze grasses and fibrous plants. Symbiotic microbes in the cecum ferment plant cellulose, enabling hindgut digestion without a ruminant’s multi-chambered stomach.
sections.behavior: Horses are social: free-ranging mares and offspring form stable family bands, while young or unattached males may gather separately. Domestic herds also form preferred bonds. Horses communicate through senses, posture, and calls, and often graze or rest together.
sections.reproduction: Mares generally cycle in long-day seasons. Pregnancy averages about 340 days, or eleven months, with variation. Usually one foal is born; it soon stands, follows its mother, and nurses as she protects it.
sections.ecology: Grazing removes plants and can change habitat. At springs in Nevada’s Great Basin, plots accessible to feral horses had less plant cover and species richness than horse exclosures. In high-elevation meadows, protected vegetation was taller than vegetation grazed by horses and cattle. These local results depend on habitat and grazing pressure.
sections.conservation: Domestic horses are maintained through breeding, not as a wild population. Breeds vary in size, build, coat, and inherited traits selected for different uses and conditions. Preserving distinct breeds maintains domestic diversity; a wild equid’s conservation status does not describe domestic horses.
